LINCOLN, Neb. (KOLN) - A new online teaching program has launched in Nebraska this month called Teachers of Tomorrow, aimed at giving those interested in a teaching certificate an alternative prep program.

The fully online program is meant to be flexible and is designed for those who already have a bachelor’s degree and want to become a teacher without going back to a four-year college.

Chief Growth Officer Alex Elson said if anyone is looking for a career switch to a teacher, this is a good option to stay in their role while preparing for that change.

“This could be a pharmacist or a banker. It’s designed for a paraprofessional who has a four-year college degree, but may be interested in moving into a full time classroom teaching position. It’s for that recent grad in Lincoln who says I now need to pursue teacher certification,” Elson said. “Anyone who is interested in stepping into the classroom to serve students is eligible for this program.”

Teachers of Tomorrow has already been used nationally for more than 20 years in other states such as Texas, Missouri and Michigan. The Nebraska Department of Education recently approved it to certify teachers in the Cornhusker State.

This comes at a time when Nebraska is facing a teacher shortage, with 490 positions left unfilled by fully qualified personnel in the 2025-26 school year, according to a Nebraska Department of Education survey.

Elson said officials are already meeting with districts across the state to identify Nebraska’s high-need areas and how best to fill vacancies.

“By preparing new teachers to step into classrooms, we hope that that will offset the burden for teachers who are in classrooms with disproportionate student to teacher ratios,” he said. “We want to be an active partner with traditional four year programs, with other alternative certification programs, to address the concerning teacher vacancy crisis.”

Elson said aspiring educators can get through the coursework in as little as a year, but can stay in the program for as long as three years. The hope is to make them eligible for placement within the same year they enroll.

Applicants can submit an application on the Teachers of Tomorrow website.
